title: Lesson 2.4 Knowledge Check
description: Five questions on evaluating AI feedback and the ethics of staging AI-assisted theater. Unlimited attempts; your best score counts.

questions.text: An AI note says "raise the stakes and develop the characters more" without pointing to any line. How should you classify it?
questions.feedback: Feedback that could apply to any scene and points nowhere is generic. Ask the model to locate it; if it cannot, discard it.

questions.text: Which prompt is most likely to produce useful feedback?
options: Read as a dramaturg preparing first-rehearsal notes. Comment only on objective, obstacle, and subtext. Give five notes, each quoting the line it refers to.
Rewrite this scene to be better
questions.feedback: Specify the lens, the criteria, and the form. Then ask the model which notes it is least confident about.

questions.text: Which are among the five ethical questions this lesson raises about staging AI-assisted theater? Select all that apply.
questions.feedback: Authorship, consent, representation, labor, and disclosure.

questions.text: Because a text model produces feedback instantly and confidently, its notes should be treated as more reliable than a peer's.
questions.feedback: Fluency is not accountability. The model has no stake in your work and no knowledge of your room; classify every note before acting on it.

questions.text: According to this lesson, what is the one clearly wrong approach to the ethics of staging AI-assisted work?
options: Crediting the model in the program
Not asking the questions at all
questions.feedback: Reasonable people reach different positions. The only wrong approach is to skip the questions.
